name: Russia
system: Federal semi-presidential republic (dominant-party, highly centralised presidency)

legislature.name: State Duma (lower house, 450)
legislature.detail: United Russia 349 seats after Sept 2026 election; CPRF 37, LDPR 23, New People 19, A Just Russia 17.

legislature.name: Federation Council (upper house)
legislature.detail: Appointed by regional authorities; chaired by Valentina Matviyenko.

judiciary: Constitutional Court and Supreme Court; judicial appointments controlled by the presidency and widely regarded as lacking independence.

elections.name: State Duma election
elections.note: Held 18–20 Sept; United Russia won a record 349 seats. No OSCE observers invited.

synopsis: Power is concentrated in the presidency, with United Russia dominating parliament and organised opposition largely suppressed. Policy is centred on the war in Ukraine, a war-oriented economy and confrontation with the West.
policies: Continuation of the war in Ukraine and negotiation on Russian terms
Military-industrial expansion and high defence spending
Pivot of trade and energy exports toward China, India and the Global South
Tight control of media, internet and civil society
challenges: Western sanctions and lower energy revenues
Inflation, high interest rates and labour shortages

name: China
system: Unitary one-party socialist republic led by the Chinese Communist Party

headOfState.name: Xi Jinping
headOfState.title: President; CCP General Secretary; CMC Chairman

governingParties: Chinese Communist Party (with eight subordinate 'democratic parties')

legislature.name: National People's Congress (~2,900)
legislature.detail: Meets annually each March; Standing Committee chaired by Zhao Leji.

judiciary: Supreme People's Court; courts operate under Party leadership via the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission.

elections.name: 20th Party Congress
elections.note: Xi secured a third term as General Secretary.

elections.name: 21st Party Congress
elections.note: Expected autumn 2027; leadership reshuffle and Xi's possible fourth term.

synopsis: Xi Jinping has consolidated power to a degree unseen since Mao, with the Party firmly over state institutions. Priorities include technological self-reliance, national security and managing a slowing economy under the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030).
policies: 15th Five-Year Plan: advanced manufacturing, AI and semiconductor self-sufficiency
Boosting domestic consumption amid deflationary pressure
Assertive posture on Taiwan and the South China Sea
Anti-corruption campaigns, including within the military
challenges: US export controls and trade tensions

name: Japan

legislature.name: House of Representatives (465)
legislature.detail: LDP won ~315 seats in the Feb 2026 snap election, a record; with Ishin (36) the bloc holds ~351.

legislature.name: House of Councillors (248)
legislature.detail: LDP lacks an upper-house majority, limiting but not blocking legislation.

judiciary: Independent Supreme Court; justices appointed by the Cabinet and subject to popular review.
synopsis: Japan's first female prime minister leads a conservative LDP government strengthened by a landslide in February 2026. Her agenda centres on economic security, defence build-up and fiscal stimulus.
policies: Defence spending increase and security cooperation with the US
Economic security and strategic industries (chips, AI)
Fiscal stimulus and cost-of-living measures
Debate on constitutional revision
challenges: Rising cost of living and weak yen

name: Israel

legislature.name: Knesset (120)
legislature.detail: The Knesset dissolved on 17 July 2026; the outgoing right-religious coalition governs in a caretaker capacity.

judiciary: Supreme Court with strong judicial review; the government's judicial overhaul remains a central political fault line.

elections.name: Knesset election
elections.note: First on-schedule election since 1988; coalition talks will follow.

synopsis: Netanyahu's right-wing and religious coalition heads into the 27 October 2026 election after the Gaza war and regional conflict. The vote will decide whether he can form a sixth government.
policies: Security policy toward Gaza, Lebanon and Iran
Judicial reform
Expanding normalisation with Arab states
Ultra-Orthodox military service exemptions
challenges: Post-war Gaza governance and hostage aftermath
reviewNote: Election on 27 Oct 2026 — update with results and coalition formation.

name: Saudi Arabia

headOfState.name: Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
headOfState.title: King and Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques

legislature.name: Consultative Assembly (Shura Council, 150)
legislature.detail: Advisory body; no legislative authority independent of the monarch.

judiciary: Sharia-based courts under the Supreme Judicial Council; the King is the final court of appeal.

elections.name: Municipal council elections
elections.note: Only national-scale elections are partial municipal votes; no national elections scheduled.

synopsis: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman runs day-to-day governance and is driving the Vision 2030 diversification programme. Social liberalisation has gone alongside tight political control.
policies: Vision 2030 economic diversification and giga-projects
Hosting Expo 2030 and the 2034 FIFA World Cup
OPEC+ oil-output management
Regional diplomacy and conditional normalisation with Israel
challenges: Fiscal pressure from lower oil prices
